source_snapshot.procedure: Connect, remove and replug the dedicated BMC cable while checking WebUI, `lan print` and one bound LAN channel.
source_snapshot.criteria: Same IP/MAC configuration and working network in all three states.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO due to physical recabling; suggests read-only `lan print` after operator changes.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED because an alternate observation/failover path and removed-state result are undefined.

old_problem: The prior result made the topology branch itself an engineering decision and treated the inaccessible private script as part of the semantic block, though a safe state matrix can represent both dedicated-only and supported shared-failover designs.
disposition_reason: Unplugging the dedicated cable must remove that physical path. The Project SPEC then selects either expected management loss with local evidence or failover over a named shared/alternate path; configuration identity persists in both. Reconnection must restore the dedicated path and, if applicable, deterministic failback. The script remains a versioned package prerequisite, not a basis for inventing behavior.
decision_basis: XLSX row 826, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2 and historical record were directly inspected.
The dedicated interface, failover mux and bound-channel policy are OEM/project behavior and must come from the physical/logical topology.
A fresh response after unplugging cannot prove dedicated-NIC operation; switch/link/route evidence must attribute it to the named alternate path.
The referenced private script content was not available, so no command or assertion is inferred from its URL; ED-36 treats that as an execution package gate.

test_case.test_name: Verify dedicated BMC NIC identity, loss/failover and restoration across a physical cable cycle
test_case.purpose: Prove the labelled dedicated management path owns the approved channel/MAC/IP when connected, becomes physically unavailable when unplugged, follows the project's dedicated-only or shared-failover contract while absent, and returns to stable dedicated service after replug without duplicate bindings.
required_package: Chassis dedicated/shared port, switch/VLAN, BMC interface/channel and MAC/IP topology
Explicit dedicated-only or named failover branch with active-channel and failover/failback deadlines
Local console or independent observer surviving dedicated-link removal
Pinned commit/archive and hash of the private dedicated-nic script with offline action/assertion/safety review, or an approved manual equivalent with coverage difference
Qualified operator, protected BMC access and physical restore procedure
test_case.test_command: Trace the chassis dedicated port to its switch/VLAN and capture baseline link, channel, route, ARP/neighbor and fresh authenticated BMC transactions. A human unplugs only the dedicated cable. Prove the dedicated switch/PHY link and traffic cease, then inspect stored channel/MAC/IP from the independent observer. For dedicated-only, verify remote loss is confined to the removed path; for approved failover, prove fresh traffic appears on the named shared/alternate switch port and bound channel within deadline. Replug, observe link training and verify dedicated service/failback plus the original identity. Do not run the private script until its exact revision is reviewed.
test_case.expected_result: Connected state uses the mapped dedicated link, one approved bound channel and expected identity. Removed state has no dedicated-link traffic while stored MAC/IP remains; it is unreachable in dedicated-only mode or reachable only through the named alternate in failover mode. Replug restores dedicated reachability and any required failback within the approved deadline, with no simultaneous unintended binding, duplicate IP, stale neighbor or BMC health error.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires operator cable evidence, switch/PHY loss and return, configuration persistence, path-attributed fresh transactions matching the selected branch, correct channel/MAC/IP and stable recovery. A cached WebUI/lan-print response is not reachability proof. FAIL includes traffic claimed on an unplugged dedicated link, unexplained alternate response, wrong channel/MAC/IP, loop/duplicate address, missing expected failover, failure to return/fail back, or inability to restore. An unreviewed script cannot contribute PASS evidence.
safety_gate: Human verifies and handles only the labelled dedicated cable
Maintain local/alternate recovery before removal; never rely on the tested path as sole observer
Prevent shared/dedicated loops, duplicate addresses and accidental production-port changes
Use protected credentials and require path attribution for every transaction
Stop on wrong path, network storm, BMC loss or failed replug/failback; no automatic cable cycle or script execution
expected_evidence: Serial-bound port/channel/switch/VLAN/MAC/IP topology and selected branch
Pinned script content/hash/review or approved non-script coverage statement
Baseline dedicated link/channel and fresh transaction evidence
Removal timestamp, switch/PHY loss and local stored-configuration evidence
If failover: alternate-port MAC learning/channel/transactions and timer
Replug/link-training/failback timeline, final neighbor/routes and BMC health
test_case.recovery: Stop on mis-cabling, loop, duplicate response or management loss. Reconnect and secure the traced dedicated cable, restore the approved switch/VLAN and interface policy from local/OOB access, clear only stale client neighbor state when approved, and verify the exact BMC identity. Do not run or retry the private script automatically.

source_conflict.preserved_original_conflict: Master requires network operation while its named dedicated cable is absent and does not identify an alternate path.
source_conflict.resolution: Make dedicated-link loss mandatory and use the authoritative topology to select either expected remote loss or named alternate failover; both preserve configuration checks.

blocked.reason: The functional oracle is valid for both supported topology branches; the exact path, timer and script revision are readiness inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Dedicated/shared topology, channel/MAC/IP map, selected failover branch/timers, observer and pinned script package.
